qc-05-c1.text: Peter W. Shor (1995). Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Prime Factorization and Discrete Logarithms on a Quantum Computer. arXiv.
qc-05-c1.quote: These algorithms take a number of steps polynomial in the input size, e.g., the number of digits of the integer to be factored.
qc-05-c1.claim: Shor's algorithm (1994) factors an n-bit integer N in time polynomial in n.

qc-06-c3.text: Jarrod R. McClean, Sergio Boixo, Vadim N. Smelyanskiy, Ryan Babbush, Hartmut Neven (2018). Barren plateaus in quantum neural network training landscapes. Nature Communications / arXiv.
qc-06-c3.quote: the probability that the gradient along any reasonable direction is non-zero to some fixed precision is exponentially small as a function of the number of qubits.
qc-06-c3.claim: The most painful issue is the barren plateau phenomenon (McClean et al., 2018): for sufficiently expressive random circuits, gradients of E(θ) vanish exponentially in the number of qubits.

qc-09-c3.text: John Preskill (2018). Quantum Computing in the NISQ era and beyond. Quantum / arXiv.
qc-09-c3.quote: Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) technology will be available in the near future.
qc-09-c3.claim: John Preskill's 2018 term NISQ, Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum, describes the current hardware era

qc-08-c2.text: Rajeev Acharya et al. (Google Quantum AI) (2024). Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold. Nature / arXiv.

qc-02-c3.text: Ji-Gang Ren, Ping Xu, Hai-Lin Yong, et al (2017). Ground-to-satellite quantum teleportation. Nature / arXiv.
qc-02-c3.quote: Here, we report the first quantum teleportation of independent single-photon qubits from a ground observatory to a low Earth orbit satellite - through an up-link channel - with a distance up to 1400 km.
qc-02-c3.claim: via satellite (China's Micius, 2017, ground-to-satellite over distances up to 1,400 km)
